content.title: About
content.content: Beef NFS (non‑fabricated sort) is a whole cut of meat from cattle that has not undergone additional processing. It offers a rich flavor, firm texture and is suitable for grilling, roasting, braising and pan‑searing.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Beef is one of the most widely consumed meats worldwide.
It contains more iron than most other meats, making it a valuable source of this mineral.
NFS cuts are often chosen by restaurants for steaks because they retain the natural taste and juiciness.
The color of beef can vary with myoglobin levels; darker meat indicates higher myoglobin content.
Beef is rich in creatine, which supports muscle energy metabolism.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Beef provides complete protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Rich in iron
items.content: Heme iron from beef is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: Source of vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 is crucial for nervous system health and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Contains zinc
items.content: Zinc supports immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Creatine and carnitine
items.content: These compounds help improve endurance and energy metabolism.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beef.

items.title: High saturated fat content
items.content: Excessive intake can contribute to elevated cholesterol levels.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: Undercooked beef may harbor pathogens such as E. coli or Salmonella.

items.title: Purine content
items.content: High purine levels can exacerbate gout symptoms.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Beef can be grilled, roasted, braised, boiled or used in stews. For steaks, let the meat reach room temperature before cooking and aim for the desired doneness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store beef in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C in its original packaging or an airtight container for up to 3‑5 days. For longer storage, freeze at –18 °C; thaw in the refrigerator rather than at room temperature.

content.title: About
content.content: Custard is a dessert made from eggs, milk, and sugar, thickened by gentle heating. It has a smooth, creamy texture and a mildly sweet flavor, often flavored with vanilla, cinnamon, or fruit purées.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Custard has been known since ancient times; the earliest recipes appear in Roman cookbooks.
Traditional English custard is made only with eggs, milk, and sugar, without any starch.
In the United States, “thickened custard” often includes corn starch for a firmer consistency.
Custard is frequently used as a filling for pies, tarts, and éclairs.
Savory custard, made with cheese, herbs, and spices, is served as a side dish in many cuisines.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Eggs, the main ingredient, provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of vitamin D
items.content: Milk contributes vitamin D, which supports bone health and the immune system.

items.title: Contains calcium
items.content: Calcium from milk helps strengthen teeth and bones.

items.title: Provides B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs supply B2 and B12, important for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Easily digestible energy source
items.content: The combination of simple carbs and protein makes custard a quick and sustained source of energy.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to eggs, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Traditional sweet custard contains a notable amount of sugar, which can contribute to weight gain and blood‑glucose spikes.

items.title: Risk of bacterial contamination
items.content: If not heated properly, eggs may not be fully pasteurized, increasing the risk of salmonella.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People with lactose intolerance may experience discomfort after consuming milk‑based custard.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Custard can be served chilled or warm as a dessert, used as a filling for pastries, drizzled with fruit, berries, or caramel sauce. It can be prepared on the stovetop, in the microwave, or in a steam bath.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store prepared custard in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portions; thaw in the fridge before serving.

egg-salad-made-with-light-italian-dressi.title: Egg Salad with Light Italian Dressing

content.title: About
content.content: Egg salad with light Italian dressing is a classic dish made from hard‑boiled eggs, finely chopped vegetables, and a dressing of olive oil, vinegar, lemon juice and aromatic Italian herbs. The recipe first appeared in 1962 and quickly became popular for its light, refreshing flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first published recipe showed up in U.S. cooking magazines in 1962.
The light Italian dressing typically includes oregano, basil and garlic, giving the salad a distinct Mediterranean aroma.
Egg salad is often used as a filling for sandwiches and wraps.
Variations may add celery, scallions or capers for extra bite.
The dish stays fresh in the refrigerator for up to 3 days, making it convenient for make‑ahead meals.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Eggs provide a complete source of protein essential for tissue repair and muscle maintenance.

items.title: Healthy fats
items.content: Olive‑oil‑based dressing supplies monounsaturated fats that support heart health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs are rich in B12, riboflavin and folate, important for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Herbs and lemon juice add vitamin C and polyphenols that help combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Digestive ease
items.content: A light dressing without mayonnaise reduces saturated fat content, making the salad easier on the stomach.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals are allergic to egg proteins and must avoid the dish.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Improperly cooked or stored eggs can harbor salmonella; always fully hard‑boil eggs and keep the salad refrigerated.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Eggs contain cholesterol; people with high cholesterol should consume in moderation.

items.title: Acidic dressing
items.content: Vinegar and lemon juice may irritate the stomach of those with gastritis or ulcers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad chilled as a standalone dish, alongside bread or crackers, or use it as a sandwich filling. Garnish with fresh herbs, cherry tomatoes or olives for extra color.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Add a splash of fresh dressing before serving if needed to refresh the flavor.

content.title: About
content.content: Whiting (also known as pangasius) is a mild‑flavored white fish commonly used in cooking. When fried, it develops a golden crust while keeping a tender, flaky texture and a characteristic sea taste. It is usually served hot as a standalone dish or as part of fast‑food meals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whiting belongs to the carp family and is found in both freshwater and coastal waters worldwide.
Fried whiting is popular in Asian, European, and North American cuisines.
Proper frying retains most of the fish’s nutrients, including omega‑3 fatty acids.
The fish is often used in fish cakes, fish‑and‑chips, and as a filling for sushi rolls.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Whiting provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: The fish contains polyunsaturated fats that support heart and vascular health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Whiting supplies vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It is a source of selenium, iodine, and phosphorus, which aid thyroid function and bone health.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: When fried moderately, whiting remains relatively low‑calorie compared with many other fried foods.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to seafood, including whiting.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination
items.content: Depending on the source, the fish may contain traces of mercury or cadmium; choose reputable suppliers.

items.title: Over‑cooking
items.content: Excessive frying can produce acrylamide, a potentially harmful compound.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Added salt or sauces can raise sodium levels, which is a concern for hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Fry whiting in vegetable oil until golden, serve with lemon, tartar sauce, or vegetable sides. It can be added to salads, sandwiches, or used as a sushi roll filling.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked fried whiting in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze in a sealed bag for up to 2 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of 75 °C before serving.

content.title: About
content.content: Mixed vegetable juice is a ready‑to‑drink beverage made from a blend of fresh vegetables such as carrots, beetroot, tomatoes, cucumber and celery. The juice contains no added sugar, preservatives or artificial flavors, preserving the natural taste and nutrients of the vegetables.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Vegetable juices typically contain more B‑vitamins than most fruit juices.
The fiber content in vegetable juice helps support healthy digestion.
The vegetables used in the blend are often sourced locally, reducing the product’s carbon footprint.
The dark color of the juice comes from high levels of antioxidants like beta‑carotene and lycopene.
Vegetable juice is frequently recommended to athletes for electrolyte replenishment.

items.title: Rich in vitamins A and C
items.content: Vitamin A supports vision and immunity, while vitamin C boosts the body’s antioxidant defenses.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and supports normal heart function.

items.title: Contains folate
items.content: Folate is essential for DNA synthesis and is especially beneficial for pregnant women.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Vegetable juice provides a feeling of fullness with relatively few calories, making it suitable for weight management.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Beta‑carotene, lycopene and other phytonutrients protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Allergy to individual vegetables
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to tomatoes, celery or carrots.

items.title: High sodium content if salt is added
items.content: Some commercial versions may contain added salt; choose a no‑salt option when possible.

items.title: Possible pesticide residues
items.content: If the vegetables are not organic, trace amounts of pesticides may be present in the juice.

items.title: Not suitable for infants under 1 year
items.content: Due to potential bacterial content and acidity, the juice is not recommended for babies.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Mixed vegetable juice can be enjoyed chilled as a refreshing drink, incorporated into culinary recipes such as sauces, marinades or smoothies. For extra flavor, add a splash of lemon juice or ginger.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the juice in the refrigerator at 2‑4 °C in its sealed container. Once opened, consume within 3‑5 days. Do not freeze, as this may alter texture and taste.

content.title: About
content.content: Pancake Syrup Light is a gently sweetened, low‑sugar syrup designed for drizzling over pancakes, waffles and crepes. It has a subtle vanilla‑caramel aroma that enhances the dish without overpowering the batter, making it suitable for diet‑conscious eating.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The Light version contains roughly 2‑3 times less sugar than regular pancake syrup.
It is sweetened with natural low‑calorie sweeteners such as stevia or erythritol, making it friendly for blood‑sugar management.
No artificial colors or flavors are used.
The syrup dissolves smoothly in both hot and cold preparations, without crystallizing.
Packaging is made from recyclable plastic to reduce environmental impact.

items.title: Low Sugar Content
items.content: Helps prevent rapid spikes in blood glucose, beneficial for people with pre‑diabetes or diabetes.

items.title: Natural Sweeteners
items.content: Stevia and erythritol provide antioxidant benefits and do not affect blood sugar levels.

items.title: Free of Artificial Additives
items.content: Absence of synthetic colors and flavors reduces liver and digestive system load.

items.title: Supports Hydration
items.content: Contains a small amount of electrolytes that aid in maintaining fluid balance.

items.title: Convenient Use
items.content: Its thin consistency allows quick, even distribution over dishes without extra effort.

items.title: Allergy to Sweeteners
items.content: Some individuals may react to stevia or erythritol.

items.title: Artificial Flavor Trace
items.content: In rare cases, minimal amounts of flavorings may be present, which could cause sensitivity.

items.title: Caloric Content
items.content: Although lighter than regular syrup, it should still be consumed in moderation.

items.title: Post‑Opening Storage
items.content: Extended storage after opening can lead to microbial growth; use within 3‑4 weeks.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Drizzle the syrup over hot pancakes, waffles or crepes just before serving. It can also be mixed into batter for a gentle sweetness, used as a base for fruit sauces, or blended with yogurt.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the syrup in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, refrigerate and use within 1 month. Discard if the smell or taste changes.
